clue.text: Surprisingly opposed to bookies' judgement

blocks.note: to be against something is to be opposed to it
bookmakers express their judgement of a contest as the odds they offer

explanation.surface: Someone, to their surprise, finds themselves disagreeing with the bookmakers' verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the rest reads literally: something achieved against the odds defied the bookies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening against the odds happens despite expectation, so the phrase works as an adverb meaning unexpectedly.

clue.text: Goodbye to the Germans …

blocks.note: surface reading: bidding farewell to some German people
setter's reading: the word Germans themselves use for goodbye

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue for the surface only; this clue stands alone. 'To the Germans' means 'in German', not 'addressed to Germans'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase literally means 'until we see again', the standard farewell in that language.

clue.text: … if trial trip leads to emergency transport

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble and fall over, so the letters before it tumble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A test journey turns into a rescue mission, continuing the German farewell before it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a noun for a journey, the trial trip, but it is the verb signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift carries people or supplies by aircraft, typically in a crisis, so it is transport used in an emergency.

clue.text: Be rough in shaking guy next door

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles it up, so the letters preceding it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Advice to be rough when roughing up the man living next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the material: BE ROUGH IN has exactly nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living beside you, the guy next door.

clue.text: Vitamin B is unfortunately a hit in the Middle East setting

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters next to it come out in the wrong order
a setting holds a jewel, so the region named surrounds the little word before it

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange
ME is the standard abbreviation for the Middle East
taken as written, held inside the region

explanation.surface: A news-style line about an unlucky strike somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the hit in the region; instead it is two letters that the region's abbreviation wraps around, after the shuffled A HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamine is the chemical name of vitamin B1, one member of the B group of vitamins.

clue.text: Has hidden desire for the scavengers

indicators.note: to have something hidden is to hold it out of sight inside, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: taken as written, split around the inner piece
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Someone harbours a secret longing for animals that live off carrion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' suggests the answer is hidden in the clue's letters, but here it means one word holds another.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are African carnivores well known for feeding on carcasses killed by other predators, making them typical scavengers.

clue.text: Musical group starts out cold, then eventually thaws

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of out
opening letter of cold
opening letter of then
opening letter of eventually
opening letter of thaws

explanation.surface: A band's performance begins frosty before the audience gradually warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts out cold' reads as one phrase about a frosty start, but 'out' is the first of the five words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight musicians performing together, a kind of musical ensemble.

clue.text: One who does not complain if daughter has untidy room at the end

indicators.note: something untidy is in disorder, so the letters of the word after it are jumbled

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written, letters to rearrange
the little word at, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A parent who tolerates a daughter's messy bedroom without complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat, figuratively, is a submissive person who lets others walk all over them without protest.

clue.text: School kids stayed awake, knowing their place

blocks.note: a class is a group of pupils taught together
someone who stays awake remains conscious

explanation.surface: Pupils who managed not to doze off in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing their place' is the British sense of being aware of one's position in the social hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being class-conscious means being acutely aware of social rank, like someone who knows their station in society.

clue.text: Make fruitful while fire is let out

indicators.note: a fire let out spreads and scatters, so the letters before it are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Farmers burning off stubble to enrich the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To fertilise land or a plant is to make it productive, enabling it to bear crops or seed.

clue.text: Go fishing with ugly dwarf

blocks.note: first meaning: to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat
second meaning: a hideous creature from Scandinavian folklore

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fishing trip with an unattractive companion; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb names a fishing method with a trailed line; the noun names a misshapen folklore being, often a giant or dwarf.

clue.text: Flag in front of hotel indicates nationality

indicators.note: one thing coming in front of another means the first word's letters lead and the second's follow

blocks.note: a flag is a plant of the iris family, like the yellow flag
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The flag flying outside a hotel tells you which country it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a national banner, but it is the flower: wild irises are called flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is the nationality of a person from Ireland, used here as a noun naming that citizenship.

clue.text: Lunch and breakfast or tea stirred with another slimmer? Not right!

indicators.note: not right tells you the abbreviation for right must be removed from the word in question
stirring mixes ingredients together, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before losing one letter

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether stirring tea with a fellow dieter is the right way to take meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R (right) from SLIMMER, then shuffle what is left with TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch and breakfast are both set times of day for eating, so together they are examples of mealtimes.

clue.text: Making one's mark in a repetitive sense

definitions.text: Making one's mark in a repetitive sense

blocks.note: surface reading: becoming well known or successful
setter's reading: writing the small marks that mean 'the same again' beneath an item in a list

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making one's mark' is an idiom for achieving distinction, but here the mark is a literal one: the pair of commas used to repeat the line above.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditto is to repeat what has gone before, and in writing it means putting ditto marks under a repeated entry.

clue.text: Feverish from the cold, perhaps, I caught

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding letters are only possibly in this order, and may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written
c. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone explains that they came down with a fever after catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I caught' reads as the speaker catching the cold, but 'caught' is the cricketer's C. 'Hectic' originally described the flushed fever of consumption.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic first meant feverish, describing a recurring fever such as accompanied tuberculosis, before it came to mean frantic.

clue.text: China deal cooked up over Mexican fast food

indicators.note: something cooked up is concocted or invented, so the letters before it are recombined

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A trade agreement with China hatched over a quick Mexican meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce, a staple of Mexican takeaway and street food.

clue.text: Wrote music that was calm

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of the verb for creating musical works
second meaning: an adjective for being collected and unruffled

explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes a peaceful piece of music; the two halves are a verb and an adjective spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer composes music, so the past tense fits; a composed person is serene and self-possessed.

clue.text: Stay outside or at a holiday town

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: to rest is to remain or stay
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between staying outdoors or at a seaside town for the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction offering a choice, but it is the two letters that go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place, often a coastal town, that people visit for holidays and leisure.

clue.text: Ordinal fraction of paradise?

definitions.note: stands for the word by itself only through the phrase seventh heaven

blocks.note: first meaning: a word that is both an ordinal number and the name of a fraction, one part of seven
second meaning: the heaven of highest bliss in the phrase for perfect happiness

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'paradise' is only reached through the idiom 'in seventh heaven', meaning blissfully happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers like this double as fraction names, and the highest heaven of Jewish and Islamic tradition is the seventh.

clue.text: Simply a wooden house

blocks.note: surface reading: an adverb meaning merely, as in 'it is just a house made of wood'
setter's reading: a simple, rustic dwelling built from tree trunks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Simply' seems to play the house down, but it describes the building itself: a plain, rough-hewn hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A log cabin is a simple dwelling built of unsquared timber trunks, the archetype of a basic wooden home.

clue.text: Irish figure prohibits ambassador covering Europe

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it covers, so the ambassador wraps around the continent's letter

blocks.note: to ban is to prohibit
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
E is the standard abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: An Irish politician blocks an envoy from representing the whole of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish figure' sounds like a public person, but it is a figure of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is a female spirit in Irish folklore whose wailing foretells a death in the family.

clue.text: Too much work left over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the two pieces before it are read backwards

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone complains that there is far too much work still outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' reads as remaining, but splits into 'left' for the ship's side and 'over' for the turnaround. Troppo is Italian for too much, used in music as in 'non troppo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troppo is the Italian musical term meaning excessively, familiar from directions such as allegro ma non troppo.

clue.text: Try to overhear how the First Lady's hidden article on the Fall

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside, so the article sits within the possessive name

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, plus the possessive S
a is the indefinite article
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A riddle about how Eve secretly learned of the Fall of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, and 'the Fall' the biblical event, but they are Eve and a plain drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation, an attempt to overhear it.

clue.text: Almost falls for the lingerie

blocks.note: first meaning: loses footing briefly without quite going down
second meaning: women's undergarments hanging from the shoulders or waist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a deletion signal for the last letter of a word, but it belongs to the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who slips nearly falls over; slips are also light petticoats worn as underwear.

clue.text: One tossed coin to decide the order

indicators.note: a tossed salad or coin is thrown about, so the letters next to it are scrambled

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A captain tosses a coin to settle who bats first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The order' sounds like a batting or running order, but it is one of the classical orders of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, recognisable by the scroll-shaped volutes on its column capitals.

clue.text: Nine university doctors experiencing feelings of languor

definitions.note: plural phrase for an uncountable noun

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Nine medics at a university feeling listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a noun for the medics, but it is a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a weary listlessness born of boredom, close in sense to languor.

clue.text: It's a chip, stupid! Nothing like a nut

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters before it are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the snack in hand is a chip and nothing like a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing like' seems to deny any resemblance, but splits into 'Nothing' for the letter and 'like' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is the green-kernelled seed of a Middle Eastern tree, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Artists' case among the furniture

blocks.note: a chest is a large box or case
artists who draw are drawers, and the possessive is expressed as 'of'

explanation.surface: An artists' carrying case lost among the furniture in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' here means people who draw, not sliding boxes, though the answer uses the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers is a piece of bedroom furniture with sliding compartments for storing clothes.
